CONFIDENCE: 0.23
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic fingerprint of an aromatic ‑NO₂ compound: NO₂ symmetric stretch doublet at 1340 & 1360 cm⁻¹, NO₂ wag at 757 cm⁻¹ and NO₂ asymmetric stretch at 1522 cm⁻¹.  A very strong band at 1426 cm⁻¹ fits CH₃ bending, indicating a methyl substituent.  The band at 661 cm⁻¹ points to an aryl-Cl (C–Cl) stretch, while the 1100 cm⁻¹ peak matches the SO₂ symmetric stretch.  
Only candidate 3 (CN(Cl)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1) simultaneously contains:  
• an aromatic nitro group (explaining 757/1340–1360/1522 cm⁻¹)  
• a methyl group (explaining strong 1426 cm⁻¹)  
• a chlorine atom attached to heteroatom, giving a C–Cl/N–Cl stretch near 660 cm⁻¹  
• a sulfone group, providing the 1100 cm⁻¹ SO₂ stretch.  
The remaining candidates lack one or more of these structural elements, so candidate 3 gives the most coherent match.
